best_for: Owners of Elegoo FDM printers, such as the Centauri Carbon or Neptune series, who want the maker's own free slicer with its printer and filament profiles ready to use.
description:
Elegoo Slicer is the free slicing program from Elegoo, a maker of 3D printers, 3D scanners, filaments and resins. Chris Hong founded the company in Shenzhen, China, in 2015, at first to sell electronics and building kits to makers and students.

Use this slicer with Elegoo's FDM printers; for its resin printers, the company offers a separate program called SatelLite. Elegoo is updating the slicer quickly, and you can join the slicer beta channel on its Discord server to hear about new features first and give feedback.

points.title: An OrcaSlicer fork, free under the AGPL
points.text: Elegoo Slicer is open source under AGPLv3 and builds on OrcaSlicer, which itself comes from Bambu Studio, PrusaSlicer and Slic3r. Release 1.5.3.4 says it merged most of OrcaSlicer 2.4.2. The project describes it as a slicer for most FDM printers, with Elegoo's own models and filaments preset.

points.title: Sending jobs to Elegoo printers
points.text: N4 and newer printers can be found automatically or added in the Devices module, and the print dialog lets you pick the target printer. N3 and older models connect through the older physical printer option. Release 1.3.0.11 also added an account login with Nexprint, for browsing and downloading models inside the app.

points.title: Windows: one 64-bit installer
points.text: This listing has a single x64 NSIS installer per version, and its record marks it as able to install silently. The README says that if it will not start you may need the Microsoft Edge WebView2 runtime and the Visual C++ 2019 x64 redistributable. A portable .zip is also published on some releases but is not listed here.

points.title: Mac: separate Intel and Apple silicon builds
points.text: Each release has an arm64 DMG for Apple silicon and an x86_64 DMG for Intel Macs; you drag the app to Applications.

points.title: Linux is early and not listed here
points.text: Releases since 1.3.0.11 include a Linux AppImage, and the project warns that Linux support is at an early stage with possible compatibility and stability problems. This listing covers Windows and macOS only.

points.title: A young project with a short history here
points.text: The README says the slicer is changing quickly. The Windows listing keeps only 2 versions, 1.5.3.4 and 1.5.3.5, and macOS keeps one, so older releases have to come from the project's GitHub page.
